variables.meaning: rotation angle, the amount of rotation; the ratio of the arc length to the radius of curvature
arc length, the distance traveled by a point along a circular path
radius of curvature of the circular path, from the center of rotation out to the point that moves
angular velocity, the rate of change of the rotation angle
linear or tangential speed of a point on the rotating object, such as a pit on the CD or the tread of a tire
the time in which the rotation Δθ takes place
centripetal acceleration, the acceleration of an object in uniform circular motion, directed toward the center of curvature
the constant speed of the object around the circle, which is also its tangential speed
the velocity of the object at the first of the two points compared, tangent to the circle there
the velocity of the object at the second point, equal in magnitude to v₁ and different in direction
the change in velocity between the two points, which points directly toward the center of curvature
the arc length between the two points whose velocities are compared
radius of the circular path
angular velocity of the object around the circle
acceleration due to gravity, the acceleration a centripetal acceleration is usually compared with
centripetal force, any net force causing uniform circular motion; it points toward the center of curvature
centripetal acceleration, the acceleration the centripetal force supplies
mass of the object moving in the circle; it cancels out of the coefficient of friction and of the banking angle
speed of the object around the curve
radius of curvature of the curve; a larger centripetal force gives a smaller r
angular velocity of the object around the curve
friction between the tires and the road, which is the whole centripetal force on a level curve
normal force of the road on the car, perpendicular to the surface
weight of the car, the gravitational force on it
static coefficient of friction between the tires and the road
angle of the banked curve, measured from the horizontal
acceleration due to gravity
angular velocity of the rotating frame: the merry-go-round, the centrifuge, or Earth itself
magnitude of the gravitational force each of two bodies exerts on the other; the two are equal, as Newton’s third law requires
gravitational constant, a proportionality factor thought to be the same everywhere in the universe
mass of the smaller of the two bodies, such as the object standing on Earth
mass of the larger of the two bodies, such as Earth
distance between the centers of mass of the two bodies
acceleration due to gravity at a distance r from the center of a body of mass M
centripetal acceleration of the Moon in its orbit, which Newton compared with the acceleration due to Earth’s gravity there
angular velocity of the Moon about Earth
period of an orbit, the time for one complete orbit
period of the first of two satellites of the same parent body
period of the second of two satellites of the same parent body
radius of curvature of the satellite’s circular orbit, its average distance from the center of the planet
average orbital radius of the first satellite
average orbital radius of the second satellite
mass of the parent body the satellite orbits
mass of the satellite, which cancels out of every result of this section
gravitational constant
orbital speed of the satellite, the circumference divided by the period
net external force on the satellite, which is the gravitational force of the parent body
centripetal acceleration of the satellite
